newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Meat says fraud at U.S. unit.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Meat says fraud at U.S. unit.

text.p: Nippon Meat Packers Inc, a large Japanese meat packing firm, said on Saturday that an official at its wholly-owned U.S. subsidiary was suspected of embezzling between $80 million and $100 million.
Company president Hiroji Ohkoso told a news conference: "We suspect one of our accountants embezzled between $80 million and $100 million."
He said the accountant in question was working at Nippon Meat Packers' wholly-owned subsidiary, Day-Lee Foods Inc, based in Santa Fe Springs, California.
"We believe this is an isolated incident and that nobody else in the company was involved. This will not result in any significant loss for the company," Ohkoso said.
He said other accountants were investigating the case, which apparently centred on bank loans secured by the accountant that were not entered into the company's books.
He said the firm would announce other details when the probe is completed.
Day-Lee Foods is involved in meat processesing as well as import and export of their products. It had sales of about $485 million in the year which ended March 1996.
Nippon Meat Packers, known in Japan as Nippon Ham, is one of Japan's three biggest companies selling hams and sausages.
